problem: The geometric series $1-\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{25}-\frac{1}{125}+\frac{1}{625}$ can be expressed using sigma notation as
worked_solution:
We must express the given series in the form

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{N}{a}_{1}{r}^{n-1},
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ denotes the first term of the series, $r$ denotes the common ratio, and $N$ denotes the number of terms in the series. In this case, ${a}_{1}=1$ and $N=5.$

To find $r,$ we calculate the ratio of the first two terms in the series:

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{2}}{{a}_{1}}=\frac{(-\frac{1}{5})}{1}=-\frac{1}{5}
$$

Therefore, expressing the given geometric series in sigma notation, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}1-\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{25}-\frac{1}{125}+\frac{1}{625} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{5}1\cdot {(-\frac{1}{5})}^{n-1} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{5}{(-\frac{1}{5})}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$
